summary: The Navesink Twin Lights, a brownstone fortress of two towers above Sandy Hook Bay, held America's first Fresnel lenses (1841), its first electric arc light (1898) and a Marconi wireless station (1899).

access.note: Museum and grounds free; towers climbable for a fee in summer season (Memorial Day to 31 October); North tower free off-season. State historic site.

notes_for_editor: Sources conflict on several points, all stated in the story: which tower held which 1841 lens; the 1862 lens arrangement (NHL vs 1931 Bulletin vs TLHS FAQ); which tower got the 1883 mineral-oil lamp; the 1898 dates (1931 Bulletin 2 June, LighthouseFriends 30 June, 1899 report 15 September for the north tower); when commercial electricity returned (1924 vs 1939); the north-tower lens now (fifth-order, sixth-order). The NHL nomination calls the first keeper Joseph in one place and Joshua in another. Whether the north tower is lit today is not settled; the record's Iso W 10s characteristic is unsourced and was left out. LighthouseFriends and TLHS pages are summarised, not copied. USLHS roster lines were imported wholesale from roster.py (including 'at least' spans); only Doty, Chadwick, Bishop, Newton, Pickell and Rockette are mentioned in the story. LighthouseFriends lists Gordon B. Sickles and Thomas Pickup 1917-1919 where the archive has Gordon D. Sickles and 1917-1918, plus William Smith/Henry Summan at 1853 differences; the archive was followed. Newspapers were not searched (the shared limiter timed out). Structure heights/types in facts partly from the NHL nomination p. 4 (south tower 53 ft); the 1828 towers' type from p. 7. No wrecks or rescues were found tied to the station in the sources read.
